lesson.title: Baptism and prayer in the Didache

readings.title: Concerning Baptism.
readings.text: 1. And concerning baptism,  thus baptize ye:  Having first said all these things, baptize into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,  in living water.  2. But if thou have not living water, baptize into other water; and if thou canst not in cold, in warm. 3. But if thou have not either, pour out water thrice  upon the head into the name of Father and Son and Holy Spirit. 4. But before the baptism let the baptizer fast, and the baptized, and whatever others can; but thou shalt order the baptized to fast one or two days before.

readings.title: Concerning Fasting and Prayer (the Lord's Prayer).
readings.text: 1. But let not your fasts be with the hypocrites;  for they fast on the second and fifth day of the week; but do ye fast on the fourth day and the Preparation (Friday).  2. Neither pray as the hypocrites; but as the Lord commanded in His Gospel,  thus pray: Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth. Give us to-day our daily (needful) bread,  and forgive us our debt as we also forgive our debtors. And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one (or, evil); for Thine is the power and the glory for ever. 3. Thrice in the day thus pray.

scripture.text:
Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.

And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

overview.text: The Didache records an early community’s arrangements for baptism, fasting, and prayer. Baptismal language names the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; fasting and repeated prayer form part of the life described. These passages document the community’s pattern of worship and initiation.
overview.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: The baptismal pattern and its stated alternatives

paragraphs.text: The text first identifies a preferred form of water and then lists alternatives when it is unavailable, including pouring in the circumstances it names. It also describes fasting involving the candidate and others before baptism. The point is the combination of a definite Trinitarian confession with practical provisions within the text’s own order.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: The Lord’s Prayer and a recurring pattern

paragraphs.text: The Didache provides the Lord’s Prayer and specifies its repetition in the community’s daily life. It also distinguishes its fasting days from those of a group it calls hypocrites. The prayer’s petitions concern God’s name and kingdom, daily provision, forgiveness, and deliverance; the source’s exact wording and schedule remain available in the original passage.
